One user was really impressed with AnythingLLM as a no-fuss way to use LLMs both locally and via APIs. They said tinkerers get a solid range of choices for embedders and vector stores, and called the single-install desktop packaging very slick.
Compared with Open WebUI: "I had a much smoother experience with the desktop version of AnythingLLM. There's more in openwebui, but the things that are in AnythingLLM are more polished (IMO)."
A user hit an error installing on Linux. They fixed it by running sudo chown root:root and chmod 4755 on the AnythingLLMDesktop chrome-sandbox file. Other than that, they said it worked really well.

Another commenter warned against the Linux chrome-sandbox workaround (chown root + chmod 4755). They said it makes chrome-sandbox run as root with access to everything, and urged finding proper permissions instead.

A user tried it on a batch of regulatory PDFs with GPT-4o and said it looks great so far. However, citations were 'a bit dicey': answers were largely correct, but the citations window showed somewhat garbled content. They also asked for text search across existing chat history.

Another user called it super easy for less technical folks and had it running in under 5 minutes. With Ollama, everything was automatically detected, while manual setup is still possible. They said adding Hugging Face was quick and painless.

One commenter praised the granular control over the LLM setup, citing three things: the ability to edit the system prompt, change the LLM temperature, and choose between open-source and closed models.

"My first reaction was 'oh great, another Ollama/WebGenUI wrapper on Llama.cpp' but it's actually much more." The commenter noted it supports embedding models, vector databases, and TTS/STT, everything needed to build a fully functioning voice chatbot.
"As someone who doesn't know what an Embed or Vector is, this has been the only offline AI tool I've been able to install and start using on my standard office PC."

A user set up AnythingLLM to trial it at the enterprise level and was super impressed with most features so far. They wished for an option to properly include custom CSS, saying the default interface looks a little dated.

A user deploying a customized AnythingLLM instance in an enterprise environment found the developers top notch and very responsive. They are waiting on EntraID integration, after which they believe it can cover most of an org's lowest-hanging use cases.
